stemMd: A worker lifts a 12 kg object vertically through 2 m at constant speed. Taking g=10 m/s², how much work does the lifting force do?
explanationMd: The lifting force balances weight mg=120 N. Its work over 2 m is 120 times 2=240 J; gravity does equal negative work, so net work is zero.

distractorRationale.d: This divides by distance instead of multiplying.
distractorRationale.e: This is the weight's numerical value without the lift distance.
distractorRationale.a: This omits gravitational acceleration in calculating weight.
distractorRationale.b: Zero net work does not mean each individual force does zero work.
